@graph.description: Data center relocation — the physical layer — from The Flat Rate Movers: servers, populated and de-racked racks and cabinets, storage and network equipment moved between server rooms, colocation facilities and data centers in Northern Virginia and the I-81 corridor as a planned, labelled, documented sequence. The crew performs disconnect and reconnect, de-install and placement — shutdown and unplug in the sequence fixed at survey with the client's IT team, and reconnection, re-cabling and power-up at the destination to the scope agreed at survey; where an element requires certified specialists, the company engages certified contractors for that element. Equipment is inventoried and manifested before anything is unplugged, packed padded, wrapped and strapped with custom crating where needed, sealed with tamper-evident seals, transported in the planned order, and placed in labelled rack and U order, physically verified with the client's team. Retired equipment is packed, sealed, manifested and hauled to the certified ITAD partner engaged for the job; data sanitization, destruction and certification belong to that partner and are never claimed by the company. Populated racks and cabinets in the 1,500–3,500 lb band are surveyed under SIR/KIM-GS with an L/360 floor check. Flat rate quoted in writing before move day. No workload migration or recommissioning is offered or claimed, and the company claims no IT certifications of its own.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to move a data center, per rack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Published 2026 market guidance spans $5,000 to $25,000 per rack for the physical relocation, and the honest sources say there is no universal per-rack price — rack weight, access, waves and parallel running move the number more than rack count alone. We do not price per rack at all: after the survey, your whole physical scope is quoted per job at one flat rate, in writing, before move day.

mainEntity.name: Who disconnects and shuts down our systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our crew does. Shutdown and unplug happen device by device, in the sequence fixed at survey with your IT team, and nothing is unplugged before it is inventoried and labelled. Where an element requires certified specialists, the company engages certified contractors for that element. The decisions about the logical move — what runs, in what order, what stays live — are made with your team at the survey; the physical disconnect and reconnect work is ours.

mainEntity.name: Do you destroy data or issue destruction certificates?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — and any mover who offers to should end the conversation. Sanitization to NIST SP 800-88 and IEEE 2883, NAID AAA-certified destruction, R2v3 recycling and serialized Certificates of Destruction belong to a certified ITAD partner. We haul your retired equipment to the certified partner engaged for the job, sealed and manifested, and reconcile the manifest with them at intake.

Populated racks are surveyed like any high-mass asset: racks and cabinets in the 1,500–3,500 lb band get the SIR/KIM-GS survey with an L/360 floor-deflection check at origin and destination, and the heaviest populated cabinet governs the floor and elevator checks. Whether a specific rack travels populated or de-racked is a survey decision, made with your team, based on the rack, the route and the floors at both ends.

mainEntity.name: Do you re-rack, cable and power systems back up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We place devices back in labelled rack and U order per the manifest, reconnect and re-cable them, and power up to the scope agreed at survey, verifying placement with your team before we leave. What stays with your IT team is recommissioning — bringing applications and services back online; we do not claim the logical layer.

mainEntity.name: How long does a relocation take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The program around the move — destination readiness, circuits, phased cutover — runs 8 to 16 weeks for a mid-market move in published guidance. Our part is scheduled inside your team’s sequence: survey and manifest first, then move days in the waves your plan sets, least critical first where the plan phases it.

The chain-of-custody manifest: asset tag, serial number as you provided it, rack and U position at origin and destination, photograph points, seal numbers verified at departure and arrival, and a signed handoff at placement — or, for retired equipment, at your ITAD partner’s intake.

mainEntity.name: Can you provide a certificate of insurance for our facility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The contractor insurance certificate is current and is provided to facility management as part of engagement setup, and additional coverage can be arranged where a project requires it.
